name: London Ambulance Service
description:
The London Ambulance Service dispatches ambulances in emergencies. The key goal is to allocate an available ambulance for every call that can reach the scene within 11 minutes. The entire dispatch process must not exceed a set maximum time limit.

To make this work, the Computer Aided Despatch system analyzes incident forms and assigns vehicles. It is vital to track the exact location of moving ambulances. This requires ambulance staff to follow standard routes and correctly communicate departure and destination information, allowing radio operators and the CAD system to record data accurately.
rawDescription:
The London Ambulance Service dispatches ambulances in emergencies. The key goal is to allocate an available ambulance for every call that can reach the scene within 11 minutes. The entire dispatch process must not exceed a set maximum time limit.

To make this work, the Computer Aided Despatch system analyzes incident forms and assigns vehicles. It is vital to track the exact location of moving ambulances. This requires ambulance staff to follow standard routes and correctly communicate departure and destination information, allowing radio operators and the CAD system to record data accurately.
highLevelGoals: Ensure that the emergency call is successfully received and the incident details are accurately captured to initiate the dispatch process.
Assess the severity and nature of the incident to determine the appropriate response and resource allocation.
Allocate an available ambulance to the incident such that it can reach the scene within the 11-minute target time.
Communicate departure and destination information accurately to allow the CAD system to record data and track the ambulance's location.
Follow standard routes to ensure predictable travel times and accurate location tracking by the dispatch system.
lowLevelGoals: The system validates the caller's identity and captures the incident type, location, and contact details into a new incident record.
The system assigns a unique incident ID and sets the incident status to 'Active' to trigger the dispatch workflow.
The system calculates a priority score based on the incident type and reported symptoms to determine the response level.
The system updates the incident record with the final priority level and required resource types (e.g., ALS, BLS).
The system queries the fleet database for ambulances that are available, within range, and equipped for the required priority level.
The system calculates the estimated time of arrival (ETA) for each candidate ambulance based on current traffic and distance.
The system assigns the ambulance with the lowest ETA that meets the 11-minute target to the incident and updates its status to 'En Route'.
The system records the timestamp and location of the ambulance's departure from the station.
The system updates the incident record with the confirmed destination address and any en-route location changes.
The system retrieves the pre-defined standard route for the assigned ambulance to ensure predictable travel times.
The system continuously updates the ambulance's GPS location in the CAD system to maintain accurate tracking.

baselineCritiques.actors: The actors listed are mostly appropriate for the described system. However, there is a redundancy between "Ambulance Crew" and "Ambulance Driver." Typically, an ambulance crew includes multiple roles (e.g., driver, paramedics), so specifying both as separate actors may not be necessary unless further differentiation is required. Additionally, the description of the system implies that the ambulance staff (crew) are responsible for following routes and communicating location, which is already covered by "Ambulance Crew." Removing one of these redundant roles would improve clarity.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The high-level goals are well-defined and align with the system's description, covering key aspects of emergency dispatch such as call initiation, incident assessment, ambulance allocation, location tracking, and route adherence. No contradictions or omissions are observed.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are well-aligned with the high-level goals and accurately reflect the functional requirements of the London Ambulance Service system. Each goal corresponds to a specific action by an actor, ensuring completeness and adherence to the GORE framework. No contradictions or omissions were detected.
